strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses important efficiency bottleneck for high-resolution diffusion model deployment
Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple architectures (DiT, SANA, FLUX), both class-to-image and text-to-image tasks, extensive ablations showing each component's importance
Strong empirical results: achieves 53× latency reduction for 4K generation with quality preservation, accomplished with modest training cost (40 H100 days)
Technically sound approach: two-stage design (embedding alignment + LoRA) is well-motivated; corrected velocity estimation properly addresses guidance-distilled model challenge
Reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters (Table 5), clear experimental setup, uses publicly available models; includes extensive supplementary results and ablations
Effective presentation: clear figures illustrating approach and results; paper generally well-organized with good flow
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (compressed autoencoders, simple MSE-based alignment, standard LoRA); lacks new insights into why approach works or theoretical characterization

Insufficient analysis of core contribution: representation gap problem identified empirically but not deeply analyzed; no formal justification for why lightweight alignment generalizes across different regimes

Narrow experimental scope: only one compression ratio effectively tested (8× VAE); no exploration of deeper compression ratios, alternative autoencoders, or other diffusion families; missing quality-speed tradeoff analysis

Missing critical comparisons: no comparison with other acceleration methods (quantization, distillation, pruning); only LoRA vs. full fine-tuning shown, not vs. other parameter-efficient methods; no training-free approaches compared

Incomplete technical treatment: guidance-distilled model correction (Eqs. 5-7) appears ad-hoc with insufficient justification; patch embedder initialization strategy unclear; hyperparameter sensitivity not analyzed
Evaluation limitations: relies solely on CLIP/FID scores without human studies or perceptual metrics (LPIPS); no analysis of semantic consistency across resolutions
Limited failure mode discussion: no explicit treatment of when approach might fail, boundary conditions, or cases with very large representation gaps; missing discussion of negative impacts

strengths: Addresses a practical and important problem: efficient high-resolution image generation with demonstrated 53× latency reduction at 4K resolution

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple architectures (DiT-XL, SANA, FLUX), resolutions (1K-4K), and datasets with thorough ablation studies (Table 6) clearly showing the contribution of each component
Well-documented implementation with detailed hyperparameters (Table 5), explicit training procedures, and reasonable reproducibility considerations
Clearly identifies and proposes a solution to the 'representation gap' problem that occurs when adapting models to new latent spaces (Figure 3-4)
Demonstrates versatility by handling different model types including guidance-distilled models with appropriate corrections (Eqs. 5-7)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Core contributions are straightforward applications of existing techniques (simple L2 embedding alignment, standard LoRA fine-tuning) without novel algorithmic insights

Weak theoretical foundation: No formal analysis of why embedding alignment solves training instability; lacks principled justification for why spatial downsampling + random initialization + L2 loss is the right approach

Insufficient comparison with related work: Despite extensive related work discussion (Section 2), provides no experimental comparison with other acceleration methods (quantization, distillation, pruning, efficient architectures) or post-training adaptation approaches

Quality-efficiency tradeoff inadequately analyzed: GenEval scores drop significantly (0.89→0.72 for FLUX; 0.82→0.72 for SANA), contradicting claims that models 'achieve quality comparable to their base models'

Critical dependency on concurrent/external work: Entire approach depends on DC-AE (refs [10,11]) as concurrent work; no discussion of applicability to other compression approaches or independence of contribution
Training cost analysis incomplete: '40 H100 GPU days' mentioned without breakdown between stages; no comparison to full retraining costs; speed benchmarks only on H100 GPU
Limited scope of evaluation: Only text-to-image generation tested; no evaluation on related tasks (editing, inpainting, ControlNet); only MJHQ-30K dataset for evaluation

Technical justification gaps: Why does Eq. (1)'s L2 loss on patch embeddings align latent spaces? Why is LoRA better than alternatives? Equation (7)'s velocity correction assumes correct distillation without validation
Reproducibility concerns: FLUX guidance-distilled weights only partially available; relies on proprietary models; no mention of code/model release
Overstated claims: Abstract claims models preserve knowledge while Table 2 shows measurable quality degradation; 'significantly more efficient' framing downplays quality tradeoffs
Missing critical analysis: No discussion of failure modes, sensitivity to hyperparameters (LoRA rank, alignment training steps), or how approach scales to larger models

strengths: Addresses a practical and important problem: achieving efficient high-resolution text-to-image generation with 53× latency reduction for 4K generation

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple architectures (DIT, SANA, FLUX.1-Krea), tasks (class-to-image and text-to-image), and resolutions (1K-4K) with both quantitative (CLIP, GenEval, FID) and qualitative results
Strong ablation studies demonstrating the importance of each component (embedding alignment, LoRA tuning, training objectives) with clear visualizations
Clear identification and analysis of the core technical challenge: representation gap between latent spaces, with concrete evidence (Figure 3) and principled solution
Sound technical approach with well-motivated design choices; the embedding alignment stage effectively bridges latent spaces before end-to-end fine-tuning
Thorough experimental methodology with detailed hyperparameters (Table 5), proper baseline comparisons, and hardware-level benchmarking on actual NVIDIA H100 GPUs
Good presentation with informative figures, particularly the pipeline diagram and visual ablations, making the approach accessible
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual technical components: embedding alignment via MSE loss is straightforward, LoRA fine-tuning is established practice, and deep compression autoencoders are prior work; main contribution is their combination
Representation gap analysis is primarily empirical; lacks theoretical justification for why latent space mismatch causes training instability or why the proposed MSE-based alignment is optimal
Missing sensitivity analysis: no exploration of how performance varies with compression ratios, patch sizes, autoencoder quality, or alternative alignment strategies beyond MSE loss
No comparison with other acceleration techniques (quantization, distillation, pruning); only compares LoRA vs full-tuning within the proposed framework, limiting context on efficiency trade-offs
Insufficient discussion of limitations and failure cases; no analysis of when DC-Gen underperforms, problematic prompt types, or what happens with mismatched autoencoder-model pairs
Autoencoder dependency underspecified: training procedures, loss functions, and architecture choices for DC-AE-I32 not detailed; sensitivity to autoencoder quality not explored
Limited scope: only evaluated on text-to-image generation (2024-2025 models); generalization to video, 3D, or other domains, and compatibility with older architectures remain unclear
Guidance-distilled model correction (Eq. 6) appears ad-hoc, suggesting unmapped edge cases in the approach; velocity estimation workaround indicates potential brittleness
Training cost of 40 H100 days is substantial but not thoroughly discussed in context of alternatives; trade-offs between pre-training cost and acceleration benefits need clearer articulation
Weak theoretical grounding: no convergence analysis, formal explanation of how lightweight alignment preserves knowledge, or formalization of the representation gap-instability connection
